question: Find the value of 5 −²³ × 16 −²³ × 21 −²³ .
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For terms with the same exponent, we can multiply the bases directly:

ax × bx × cx = (a × b × c)x

⇒ 5−²³ × 16−²³ × 21−²³ = (5 × 16 × 21)−²³

⇒ (80 × 21)−²³ = 1680−²³

⇒ 1 / 1680²³

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / 1680²³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 5−²³ × 16−²³ × 21−²³

**Formula Used:**

1) am × bm = (a × b)m

2) a−m = 1 / am

**Calculations:**

⇒ 5−²³ × 16−²³ × 21−²³

⇒ (5 × 16)−²³ × 21−²³

⇒ 80−²³ × 21−²³

⇒ (80 × 21)−²³

⇒ 1680−²³

⇒ 1 / 1680²³

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / 1680²³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Power of a Product Rule

When multiplying bases with the same exponent, you can multiply the bases first and keep the exponent intact: am × bm = (a × b)m.

Negative Exponent Rule

A negative exponent indicates the reciprocal of the base raised to a positive power: a−ⁿ = 1 / aⁿ.

Product Rule with Same Base

When multiplying terms with the same base, simply add their exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ.

Zero Exponent Rule

Any non-zero base raised to the power of zero is always equal to one: a⁰ = 1, for all a ≠ 0.
